en: In distress I saw many dreams;
Is this the sign of my champion's arrival?!
Come, Manas, give me your hand.
May I say, ‘Today I am glad’?
My peers Jakyp and Akbaltay,
Are my poor friends well?
The leaders of the exiled people,
Of the forty hearths that came to Altay,
The worthy men who would raise them up,
The shamans who strike with lungs,
They were heroes of some resource,
They were the backbone of a scattered people.
Are Akbaltay and Jakyp safe?”
Clasping hands and bounding,
These were Khan Manas's words,
To your elder, the leopard Koshoy,
This was where he answered:
“Elder, my aged Koshoy,
My resourceful saint,
My support when I pull upward,
My prop when I pull downward.
My fortunate road when I put you in front,
My san of troops when you follow behind!
My elder, my aged Koshoy—
I reckon you are he!
If you truly are my brave elder Koshoy,
Give me your coat to wear in battle.
‘I will be one who holds you as one,’ I say,
Wise Koshoy, give me your hand!
Be my support when I go out in front,
You are like a prophet,
My kingly elder, be my protector!
Truly knowing me as your lion,
Spread your palms and offer prayer.
Since the past month,
Because of news of you, elder Koshoy,
I set out willingly from Altay.
My aged one, like a prophet,
My saint whom I hold supreme,
I heard of you from Khan Akbaltay.
Spread your palms and offer your prayer,
My elder Koshoy, give your blessing!
If you give your true blessing,
The one I will fight is Kakan-Chin,
The one I will contend with is Bakburchun.
Of the unbelievers like black spiders,
I truly learned the many evil schemes,
Of those Chinese warriors.
There was torment in his words,
There was treachery in his eyes.
Angered, Esenkan
Intended to seize me.
There was something else in his words,
There was strangeness in his eyes.
Inventing another evil scheme,
That bastard Esenkan
Intended to split me apart!
There was evasion in his words,
There was distraction in his eyes.
If he had the power, Esenkan
Intended to strike me down,
Intended to dig my pit.
If he had the power, Esenkan
Was poised to spring a fine surprise.
Not letting the plow turn,
That swine made trouble,
Not letting us remain here in Altay.
His headman came to humiliate us;
Of the stone-badged Chinese,
The chosen ones assembled,
And came to oppress my father.
With their jackets puffed out,
Their mighty men came swarming:
‘The tribute livestock and Manas,
Give them to us now,’ they said,
And kept pressing my father.
Without dying and lying sprawled,
Without death coming and stretching me out,
How could I yield to his words?
While my vigorous head is still on me,
How could I give up my head!
With that dog who boasted of his strength
I clashed headlong.
There was no protector, no support,
To stand as my protector,
Like you, my leopard elder,
There was no hero to bind about my waist.
When the Chinese came to humiliate us,
And were about to ruin my settlement,
I girded my waist with a leather belt,
Against the Chinese swarming over the earth
I entered alone and attacked.
I began a mighty slaughter.
Esenkan's envoy,
His official who collected tribute,
His skilled spearmen,
His mighty men who devised plans—
I began a fierce onslaught,
Attacking all by myself,
I slaughtered his accomplished men.
The giants Kochku and Döngö died,
All who exchanged blows died.
I began a mighty slaughter;
Of the red-tasseled Chinese
I slaughtered the mightiest.
I made their braided women widows,
Their mighty men who wore jackets
I burned in fire and made ashes.
I began to heap up sorrow,
Of the monks who fell into my hands
I cut off their penises.
I brought terrible torment,
Crushing their mountainlike giants,
Ninety camels' loads of gold
I took as booty;
Thus I brought torment.
I made Altay, where I lived, a home,
I made my forty households rich.
Slaughtering livestock like a king,
‘Rich Jakyp has become wealthy,’ they said.
Hearing of his wealth, Esenkan
Said, ‘Bind his son and bring him.’
Brave Zholoy, foremost of wrestlers,
Received word from his khan.
From the city of Kakan-Chin,
When they came swarming,
The Chinese an ilek, I alone,
Had I done something for God?
The star in the sky was my guide,
Kutubiy became my companion.
Kutubiy, a support bound to my waist,
While he watched the ridge,
Brave Zholoy riding Achbuudan,
Shooting arrows like rain,
Firing bullets like hail,
His supporting force behind him
Parted as mist descended,
Their forelocks set apart,
His giants appeared behind him.
The mightiest of those giants—
Scissor-eared giant Kaman,
Vulture-tailed giant Zhoon—
When they were about to sweep over everything,
I began a fierce onslaught.
When Zholoy fled,
That great army that had come
I slaughtered entirely.
Taking my spear and wheeling it,
I drove Zholoy away.
Mottled blue clouds gathered in the sky;
Wrestler Zholoy then
Escaped by fleeing openly.
Slaughtering the Kalmyks outright,
I seized their steeds.
Against the Black Kalmyks, may they burn,
Listen, my falcon elder,
Such was the turmoil I raised.
I made their wall-felts greasy with plenty.
The forty households in Altay,
In that conflict I made them rich.
I drew my sword and made a sheath,
Against the forty Chinese tribes of Beijing
I helplessly raised a great turmoil.
I grew hardened drinking blood;
Among the Black Kalmyks and Manchus
I was named the bloodthirsty Burut.
The Chinese are countless, the Kyrgyz few;
How can their villages settle?
If we fight the Chinese to the death,
There is no forest to flee into,
Not one soul to serve as support.
What way could there be?!”
Your elder Koshoy heard,
His heart broke apart,
Choking, unable to bear it,
The tears poured from his eyes:
“Alas, Manas, what are you saying?!
Who should hear these words of yours?
Let only a dark night hear them!
Do not dig my pit, Manas,
By provoking a people with a court,
Do not make my misery boil.
Understand all that I tell you,
My lion Manas, heed my words!
Let the people of Beijing not rise,
And gather their army,
And bring humiliation upon us!
Let them not raid the four kinds of livestock,
Let the Chinese not crush us from above!
Let the Chinese not do as they please,
Let them not wipe out our lineage!
Let them not swarm from every side and hang us,
Those unbelievers, may they burn to death,
Let them not dig out every root!
Turn back and go,
Hurrying to Altay,
For now, make your way there.
Castrate the stallions and make geldings,
Castrate the rams and make wethers,
Castrate the bulls and make oxen,
The Black Kalmyks in Altay,
Daze and confound them!
Castrate the male camels and make geldings,
The troublemaking Black Kalmyks,
Leave them wholly on foot!
To those who hear and know,
Herd after herd, a plaything,
Your forty households of Kyrgyz,
Move them this way in high spirits.
The Black Kalmyks and Manchus,
When you move away clear of them,
Keeping close to the Orkon mountains,
When you rise up into view,
I will scout your road without delay.
If I, Koshoy blessed by Kydyr, do not die,
If I do not see the Last Judgment,
I will come after six months!
I have an iron coat no bullet pierces.
When the people are counted,
When the people are set down in writing,
To welcome you, my great one,
I have twelve thousand troops!
The steeds of faithful Muslims
I will set in a long procession.
Preparing coats no bullet pierces,
Preparing horses no bullet catches,
Taking land after judging its worth,
Taking men, commandeering transport,
With a road blessed by Kydyr,
All the multitudes setting forth,
I will raise a mighty commotion.
A leopard visited by Kydyr,
Your precious elder Koshoy,
From the teeming Chinese
I will free you.
When grass greens and the earth flourishes,
When fescue and sedge abound,
When the people move upward then,
When they have just reached the summer pastures,
When horses' tongues darken with green grass,
Taking seven banners and standards,
Taking an army that bends the earth,
I will go out to meet you.
Against the swarming Black Chinese,
For you yourself, my dear,
I will become a companion.
If the Black Kalmyks swarm upon us,
Standing on either side,
Firing guns and drawing bows,
Fighting with crashing blows,
Against the clattering Kalmyks,
For you, leopard Manas,
I will charge and thrust my spear.
My blood-spiller, for your sake,
Against the Black Chinese and Manchus
I will sacrifice my life.
